content:
maria: Quick heads-up — autotune run from the weekend produced some odd kernel picks for seq_len=512 on A100. Dumping a couple lines from the runtime telemetry below. Anyone seen this pattern?

kai: saw a few alerts, yes. Can you paste the specific decision lines?

maria: sure, pasted snippets: 
```
[kselect] ts=1783459001 kernel_choice=matmul_v2 kernel_id=0x3a2 reason=latency_estimate_ms(1.85)<alt(1.90) seq_len=512 arch=A100 batch=1 kv_cached=true autotune_phase=online
[kselect] ts=1783459002 kernel_choice=matmul_v1 kernel_id=0x1f4 reason=throughput_estimate(8000)<alt(8200) seq_len=64 arch=A100 batch=8 kv_cached=false autotune_phase=baseline
[kselect] ts=1783459003 kernel_choice=matmul_v2 kernel_id=0x3a2 reason=predicted_memory_pressure high seq_len=1024 arch=A100 batch=1 kv_cached=true
```

maria: note the matmul_v2 pick for 512 even though offline tests favored matmul_v1 at that seq length. Regression maybe tied to the new latency model weights.

devon: interesting — are these logs coming from the new seq-aware path (seq_path=true) or the legacy route?

maria: seq_path=true. The autotuner used the sequence-length bucketer that was merged last week.

sam: can you run the one-off with debug env flags? I want the kselect reason matrix output.

maria: running now:
```
export REDWOOD_KSELECT_DEBUG=1
export REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_MODE=seq-aware
export REDWOOD_KSELECT_PREFER_LATENCY=1
export REDWOOD_KSELECT_REASON_LEVEL=verbose
# run: ./runtest --model gpt-medium --seq 512 --batch 1 --profile
```

infra-bot: Autoscaler snapshot saved to s3://redwood-infra/autotune/snapshots/1783459012.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

kai: when you run with DEBUG=1 can you also dump the kernel microbenchmarks? We need the measured_ms vs predicted_ms table.

maria: pasted measured vs predicted from the run: 
```
kernel_id kernel_name  seq  batch  pred_ms  measured_ms  kv_cached
0x3a2    matmul_v2     512   1      1.80     1.85         true
0x1f4    matmul_v1     512   1      2.10     1.90         true
```

maria: so the predictor slightly underestimates matmul_v2 but measured still shows matmul_v1 is slightly faster at 512 in some shards — weird variance.

devon: could be memory bank conflicts specific to certain A100 firmware or CUDA driver. Do we have arch microconfig (sm_major/minor, driver version) in telemetry?

maria: yes, telemetry includes arch fields. Example: arch=A100 sm=8.0 driver=545.85. Noted a small cluster of hosts on driver 545.85, others on 545.78.

sam: try forcing an override to probe: 
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDES='0x1f4:force=1'
```
and run 50 iterations. If perf stabilizes, we can add a temporary policy to prefer matmul_v1 for seq=512 on that driver.

maria: started override test. Early results: matmul_v1 pinned gives 1.88ms median vs matmul_v2 1.92ms on same hosts.

kai: ok looks like a real regression for those hosts. We should: 1) add a short-term routing rule (prefer kernel 0x1f4 for seq in [256,768] on driver=545.85), 2) push a retrain of the latency model including driver as a feature, 3) add stricter sampling (more microbench runs) during autotune for seq buckets with high variance.

devon: agree. Also add a flag to disable seq-bucketing for the problematic driver until model retrain:
```
REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_SEQ_BUCKET_DISABLE=545.85
```

maria: filing a quick internal bug & action list. Will open a short-lived canary rollout to prefer kernel 0x1f4 on driver 545.85 and increase sampling.

infra-bot: Created issue RED-2876: "kselect: unexpected matmul_v2 picks for seq=512 on A100 driver 545.85" and scheduled canary.

sam: thanks. After canary, collect the kselect_reason histograms and attach to the ticket. We need the decision heatmap (seq vs kernel vs driver) to avoid future surprises.

maria: will do. If anyone wants the raw traces I uploaded them to the ticket. Ping me for s3 creds. :thumbsup:
